question: What three major sciences are combined in nursing informatics?
explanation: Nursing informatics merges nursing practice with computer and information systems to manage patient data effectively. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T1#GNS113_U1_T1_h1)

question: What is the main goal of nursing informatics in everyday hospital practice?

options.A: To increase the cost of hospital administrative duties
options.B: To replace bedside nurses with automated computer programs
options.C: To eliminate the need for paper prescription records
options.D: To support decision-making and improve patient safety

explanation: You got this! Technology isn't here to replace us; its ultimate aim is to empower our clinical decisions and create safer, better environments for our patients. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T1#GNS113_U1_T1_h1)

question: In informatics, what do we call raw, unorganized, and uninterpreted facts?
explanation: Think of 'data' as isolated, raw facts. They just sit there until we process them and give them some meaning! [learn more](GNS113_U1_T1#GNS113_U1_T1_h2)

question: A nurse checks a patient's vital signs and immediately spots a pattern that looks like sepsis, using past training. What level of the informatics framework is this?
explanation: Spotting a disease pattern by combining structured information with your clinical understanding is a classic example of applying your nursing knowledge! [learn more](GNS113_U1_T1#GNS113_U1_T1_h2)

question: Around which decades did computers first start showing up in hospitals for basic tasks?
explanation: Hospital computerization actually started way back in the 1960s and 1970s, mostly helping out with financial and administrative systems. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T1#GNS113_U1_T1_h3)

question: Why did early nurses push for specialized clinical software instead of just using general business programs?

options.A: General programs failed to capture unique nursing care and assessments
options.B: Hospital management forbade nurses from using standard keyboards
options.C: Business software was too expensive for Nigerian hospitals to purchase
options.D: Nurses wanted to avoid learning how to type medical notes

explanation: Standard business software just didn't cut it. Nurses needed specific tools designed to document real, hands-on professional nursing care accurately. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T1#GNS113_U1_T1_h3)

question: What is one of the main jobs of a nurse working in informatics?

options.A: Repairing broken computer monitors on the hospital ward
options.B: Acting as a bridge between clinicians and IT developers
options.C: Prescribing medications when doctors are unavailable
options.D: Managing the financial budget of the entire hospital

explanation: Nurse informaticists use their clinical know-how to translate what nurses need into technical requirements so software actually works well at the bedside. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T1#GNS113_U1_T1_h4)

question: Which skill is most essential for a nurse informaticist analyzing a busy outpatient clinic?
explanation: Workflow analysis helps identify bottlenecks in how nurses document care so technology can make processes smoother. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T1#GNS113_U1_T1_h4)

question: Which tech tool is most helpful in preventing medication errors right at the patient's bedside?
explanation: Barcode medication administration is a lifesaver—it quickly matches the patient's ID band with the drug package to stop mistakes before they happen. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T1#GNS113_U1_T1_h5)

question: How do electronic alert systems help keep patients safe on the hospital ward?

options.A: By ordering laboratory tests without physician approval
options.B: By automatically discharging patients who recover quickly
options.C: By locking computer screens when nurses walk away
options.D: By notifying staff immediately of sudden vital sign changes

explanation: Automated warnings catch patient deterioration early, giving us a helpful heads-up to step in before a crisis hits. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T1#GNS113_U1_T1_h5)

question: What is a major challenge slowing down electronic health record use in many Nigerian healthcare settings?

options.A: Strict government bans on computer usage in wards
options.B: Lack of interest from patients attending clinics
options.C: Erratic power supply and poor internet connectivity
options.D: An absolute absence of mobile phones in the country

explanation: Practical infrastructure hurdles, like unstable electricity and weak internet networks, are often the biggest roadblocks to going fully digital. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T1#GNS113_U1_T1_h6)

question: Which technology is currently helping to expand healthcare access to people living in remote rural communities?
explanation: Telemedicine is amazing for bridging the gap, using everyday communication tech to connect patients in remote areas with qualified healthcare providers. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T1#GNS113_U1_T1_h6)
